result:
## Answer

$$R_s(t,q)=q(t-1)+t+s=(q+1)(t-1)+s+1 \qquad (t>s)$$

I derived this from a lower-bound construction and checked it against two small cases. I did not prove the matching upper bound in general, so this is the value my analysis supports rather than a complete proof.

## Reasoning

**Lower bound (construction).** Take $q-1$ disjoint sets $A_1,\dots,A_{q-1}$ of size $t-1$, and a set $B$ of size $m$. Colour each edge touching $A_i$ (and not touching an earlier $A_j$) with colour $i$. Each colour class $i<q$ then has matching number at most $t-1$.

Inside $B$, take the graph $F = K_{2t-1} \cup (s-1)K_1$, coloured with colour $q$. Its matching number is $t-1$, and its complement within $B$ is a star-like graph with no $K_{s,s}$, since the $s-1$ isolated vertices cannot form a $K_{s,s}$ with the clique. Adding $s$ or more isolated vertices would create a $K_{s,s}$ between the isolated vertices and $s$ clique vertices, which is why $m = 2t+s-2$ is the maximum.

The whole graph has $N = (q-1)(t-1) + 2t+s-2 = q(t-1)+t+s-1$ vertices. It is an $s$-connector, and no colour has a monochromatic $t$-matching. So $R_s(t,q) \ge q(t-1)+t+s$.

**Checks.**
- For $s=1$, the complement must be empty, so $G=K_N$. The formula gives $q(t-1)+t+1$, which is the Cockayne–Lorimer value for $q$ colours and $t$-matchings.
- For $s=2$, $t=3$, $q=1$, the formula gives $R=7$. A case analysis via the Tutte–Berge formula shows that every 7-vertex graph with no 3-matching has a complement containing $C_4$. So the 6-vertex example $K_5\cup K_1$ is extremal, consistent with $R=7$.

ANSWER: $q(t-1)+t+s$
